US8069128B2.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach.

Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering.description: A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter that sorts messages into folders, then uses the classifier in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages for misclassification.

Classification Model.description: A model generated during the first pass analysis based on which folder each message resides and other message attributes; it resides exclusively in non-persistent memory and is purged after use.

First Message Filter.description: A message filter that previously sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store.

Second Multi-Pass Message Filter.description: A filter configured to generate a classification model based on a first pass analysis, perform a second pass to identify misclassified messages, and purge the model from non-persistent memory.

Network Device.description: A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform multi-pass message filtering actions.

Transceiver.description: A component of the network device that sends and receives data over a network.

Processor.description: A component of the network device operative to perform actions including first pass analysis, second pass analysis, displaying misclassification identification, and purging the classification model.

Message Folders.description: A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter and inspected by the multi-pass filter.

Misclassification Identification.description: A generated identification of sorted messages that might be misclassified, displayed so a user can move misclassified messages to a different folder.

Non-Persistent Memory Location.description: A memory-resident-only location where the generated classification model resides exclusively, not stored on disk or another persistent data store.

Persistent Store.description: A persistent data store where the first message filter stores first classification data.

Client Device.description: A user's device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and where the first and second passes may occur entirely.

Processor Readable Storage Medium.description: A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages.

Message.description: An email or similar item sorted into folders, analyzed for sender information, headers, subject, originating network address, contents, and attachments.

Sender Information.description: Information within messages read during the first pass, including the sender's address and whether it is in an address book associated with a recipient.

Message Headers.description: Header information within messages, including a subject, read during the first pass analysis.

Message Content.description: The contents of messages read during the first pass analysis.

Attachments.description: Attachments within messages read during the first pass analysis.

Address Book.description: An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used to analyze whether a message sender's address is present.

User.description: A person whose mail folders are scanned and who is presented a list of messages that might be misclassified so they can move messages to different folders.

Recipient.description: A recipient associated with the message folders and with an address book used in classification analysis.

Message Delivery Management Method.description: A method for managing message delivery that involves receiving messages, sorting them into folders using a first message filter, and executing a multi-pass message filter on a client device to identify messages sorted into incorrect folders.
